title.narrative: Greater Mekong Subregion East-West Economic Corridor Agriculture Infrastructure Sector Project

description.narrative:
The Greater Mekong Subregion (GMS) East West Economic Corridor (EWEC) provides a conduit for Lao agricultural surpluses to reach the neighboring countries of Thailand and Vietnam and even beyond. There is essentially unlimited demand from these countries for Lao agricultural and rural produce. Better agriculture infrastructure will enable more diversity and value addition to agricultural produce from the target provinces. This will expand sustainable livelihoods opportunities.
The Project aims to regenerate and upgrade existing but underdeveloped or outdated agriculture infrastructures in the two target provinces over a period of eight years. The proposed project is consistent with the government's sector development objectives as presented in its Seventh National Socio-Economic Development Plan (2011-2015), Strategy for Agricultural Development to 2020, Agricultural Master Plan 2011-2015, which promotes the expansion of market-oriented agricultural production in an environmentally sensitive manner. It will be a key component in the Government's new Southern Rural Development Program (SRDP), which is currently under formulation with the support of IFAD.
The design draws upon the experience of recent rural development initiatives that ADB has financed as well as rural development initiatives financed by the World Bank - Poverty Reduction Fund, and by the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) - Participatory Irrigated Agriculture Development Project (PIADP).

description.narrative: Increased agricultural productivity in the project areas

Around 72,000 people have access to improved agriculture infrastructure Achievement: 69600 Progress/Status: Substantially achieved. This outcome target is unlikely not to meet indicator the loan closing date because the total number of irrigation subprojects to be upgraded / rehabilitated was reduced at the MTR from 25 to 17 subprojects. Consequently, the total beneficiaries of improved agriculture infrastructure (both irrigation /Road/ Market) are reduced to be 70,285 people. Detail see the Appendix 3 (Table 2. People benefit from Project) Data Source: PPMS
Annual crop production statistical reports from MAF and PAFO
PCR

Intensity of rice cultivations rises from 140% in 2013 to 180% Achievement: 60 Progress/Status: Not yet achieved. Average of latest intensity in 16 subprojects collect by PPMOs/DCOs in May 2024 show only 140%. There are only 4 subproject meet the target Full hand-over of the irrigation scheme must occur before the assessment and the system needs to operate for a full year (both dry season and wet season). However, due to the late completion of infrastructures and flooding affect to damage of some Irrigation system and covering late completion effect to late hand over of O&M to WUG .. Detail of data intensity of cropping DS 2023 and WS 2023-24 is show in the Appendix 3 (Table 3. Cropping area of WS 2023 and DS 2023-24, Average Yield of and Intensity by subproject.) Data Source: PPMS
Annual crop production statistical reports from MAF and PAFO
PCR

Annual rice yield increased from 3 .0 tons/ha in 2013 to 4.5 tons/ha Achievement: 5 Progress/Status: Partly Achieved. the Latest annual rice yield (WS 2023 and DS 2023-24) in 17 subprojects collect by PPMOs/DOC in May 2025 show that average of Yield WS 2023 is 3.74 tons/ hectare and DS is 4.58 tons/ hectare. Detail of each subproject show in the Appendix 3 (Table 3.. Cropping area of WS 2023 and DS 2023-24, Average Yield of and Intensity by subproject.) The reason of not meet target due to the late completion of infrastructure improvement as well as some subproject facing affected by flooding and late recovering. Almost subproject just completed and O&M handover to WUG in 2022, 2023 and 2024. Data Source: PPMS
Annual crop production statistical reports from MAF and PAFO

Output: Improved agriculture infrastructure Indicator: Improvements to the irrigation infrastructure in 15 schemes with a total command area of 7,083 ha (i.e., the area to which the systems can physically deliver water) Achievement: 7530 Progress/Status: Achieved. The rehabilitation and upgrading completed all 17 subprojects have been completed. Total command area is 7,890 ha (DS) and 8,290 ha (WS). Detail of each subproject see the Appendix 3 (Table 3. Cropping area of WS 2023 and DS 2023-24, Average Yield of and Intensity by subproject.) visit. The Mission visited eight subprojects namely Khanthachane, Phakkha, Houaythouat, Dongboun, Dongmone, Chanlanxe, Donmuang, and Vapy neua and found that the irrigation systems are operated and well maintained. The Mission discussed farm productivity with the WUG representatives and found out that the rice yield production in their area has increased by more than 5 - 6 tons per hectare and the price is higher by two-folds. Farmers in Kan Tha Chan and Phakkha subprojects prefer to grow rice in the wet season and other crops (vegetables, cucumbers, corn, and peanuts) during the dry season integrated.
Data Source: PPMS
Subproject completion reports

Output: Increased capacity of farmers to manage and use agriculture infrastructure efficiently Indicator: 30% women are membres of WUG and WUA management committees Achievement: 30 Progress/Status: Achieved. Phase I, II and III (17 subprojects) - 19 WUG established, with 253 executive committee members which is 77 of them are female (or 30%). Detail see Appendix 3 (Table 1. WUG organization.) WUA have been dropped from DMF during MTR.
Data Source: PPMS Training completion reports

Output: Improved agriculture infrastructure Indicator: $4 million in local wages generated from the project construction activities. Local contractor will employ at least 20% women in construction. Equal pay for men and women for work equal type Achievement: $146,503 Progress/Status: Not Achieved. At end Project, in total Labor paid is about LAK 30,608,635,281 or equivalent of US $2,671,720 (based on BCEL exchange rate end of each month); Total paid for female labor is LAK 3,069,922,222 (10.03%); and for male is LAK 27,808,624,410 (90.85%). Detail see Appendix 3 (Table 5. Local labor and wages generated from the project construction). The reason that female participation not meet target is contractors are facing of lack of female labor working for construction as: - The position that women work is administrator, cleaner, and cooking only. - Local people culture (local women) are not familiar work as construction worker. - Local women more interested in agriculture work than work hard as construction worker. Project has made great effort by described and encourage communities/women to join construction working by: 1) Before commencement of construction, project was conducted kick-off meeting and invite all party (including farmer and female) to join the meeting for inform of starting of construction including job opportunities in the construction. Contractor always in collaboration with District Coordination Office and village liaisons officers conducted awareness campaign to encouraging women participate in the construction and maintenance works; 2) Project conducted meetings for 8 new recruited contractors and relevant people for informing the project's gender requirement on 26 Jun to 11 July 2022; 3) Project conducted awareness campaigns for 8 communities (8 subprojects in Salavanh and Savannakhet province) to encourage communities and women to participate in the construction and maintenance works, with 111 (58,43%) out of total 190 participants were women Jobs available announcements had been posted in all village office boards, direct contact with villagers and through village authorities in each villages to encourage both men and women from villages in the project areas to apply and working with construction companies. However, still found only very few people interested in as young people go to work in Thailand.
Data Source: PPMS
Subproject completion reports Actual value: $146,503

Data Source: PPMS Training completion reports Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Target year: 2020 Target value: Y Actual value: Not applicable

Output: Increased capacity of farmers to manage and use agriculture infrastructure efficiently Indicator: Agriculture infrastructure management and operation plans established and under implementation in all subprojects Achievement: Yes Progress/Status: Achieved. All subprojects (17 subprojects) received O&M training before hand over O&M to WUG. As part of the O&M hand over MOU, Agriculture infrastructure management and operation plans established and on the job training was conducted which is emphasized: (i) managing water and the control structures in the schemes, for improved on-farm water distribution and delivery; (ii) funding the operation and maintenance of the schemes through water fee collection; and, (iii) management of the water user fees collected. Women are confirmed to be playing a role in management of the water user groups , the Survey Team confirmed that training was provided to water user groups that helped to maximize the productivity of the irrigation infrastructure. The training emphasized: (i) managing water and the control structures in the schemes, for improved on-farm water delivery; (ii) funding the operation and maintenance of the schemes through water fee collection; and, (iii) management of the water user fees collected. Women are confirmed to be playing a role in management of the water user groups. Data Source: PPMS Training completion reports Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Target year: 2020 Target value: Y Actual value: Yes

Output: Increased capacity of farmers to manage and use agriculture infrastructure efficiently Indicator: Full cost recovery of routine O&M costs in all subprojects by June 2022 Achievement: Yes Progress/Status: Being Achieved. 8 (eight) subprojects O&M transfer to WUG completed in 2022, 1 (one) subproject O&M transfer in 2023 and 8 (eight) subprojects just hand over in 2024. During the LIC PCR Field mission see that operating collecting Water Service Fees was collected to cover maintenance and electric costs, for pumped schemes, and administration cost. However, as half of subproject O&M transfer just completed in 2024 and starting first operation season, so it is too soon for confirmation for full recovery of routine O&M costs in all subprojects.
Data Source: PPMS Training completion reports Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Target year: 2020 Target value: Y Actual value: Yes
